title: Luma competitor benchmark (Batch 3) — coverage reconciliation and evidence audit

findings.method: Six units, stated separately so each can be re-derived independently, and summed only to give the manifest one integer. (1) 14 competitor scope rows from luma-benchmark-plan.md section 2, each checked against the six Phase 2 profiles for whether a profile exists. Result: 6 profiled, 8 not, corroborated three ways — the 'competitor N of 14' line in each profile header, the '6 of 14' line in luma-feature-inventory.md, and the named list of eight in that file's Gaps and in executive-report section 10. (2) 330 feature-matrix cells = 55 feature rows across 10 capability clusters, times 6 competitor columns; the Luma column is fixed text and is excluded, as the source excludes it. Counted BY HAND from the row literals in build_inventory.py, the generator of the companion xlsx, because the xlsx itself is binary and this agent holds no shell and no spreadsheet reader. Counted TWICE on different axes as a cross-check: by cell VALUE (Yes 99, No 55, Partial 35, Unknown 141) and independently by CONFIDENCE TAG (High 98, Medium 90, Low 1, untagged 141). Both passes total 330, which is the reconciliation; a hand count can drift by one or two but cannot drift by 55, and the two passes drifting together on different axes is not a failure mode of this method. (3) 48 journey stage-cells = 6 profiled competitors times 8 stages, from the stage strength table in luma-journey-comparison.md; 11 are Unknown, so 37 carry a rating. (4) 14 opportunity score totals in luma-opportunity-scoring.md, each re-added from its five criterion scores. ALL FOURTEEN AGREE with the stated total; no arithmetic error was found in the scoring, which is why no F-finding covers it. (5) 5 designated re-verification tests — the four prior claims in benchmark-plan section 5 plus the standing open question about Expedia's assistant — each traced to the profile or inventory row that either settles it or does not. Result: 2 of 5 settled. (6) 48 source files in research/sources/luma-competitor-analysis/ counted against research/sources-manifest.json, which records 49 files across the WHOLE of research/sources/, one of which (coforge-home.png) is outside this folder. 14 + 330 + 48 + 14 + 5 + 48 = 459. found = 10 findings, F-01..F-10 in the payload's 'Arithmetic defects' section, of which F-01..F-05 are mechanically checkable by anyone holding the same files. NOT DONE and not claimed: no sha256 was recomputed (no shell); the xlsx, both .docx files and the .pdf were never opened as binaries; the prior-art docx was not read at all; the Figma board png exceeds the image read limit. Each is carried in the payload's Gaps table, not netted out of the denominator.

notes.tokens_version_is_null_deliberately: This is a prose research document about a third-party travel study. It references no design token, no CSS custom property and renders no colour, so null is the TRUE value and not an unfilled field. Setting a release here would manufacture the false provenance that audit-system.py check 5f exists to prevent, and the check treats both directions as errors.
notes.why_two_artifacts: The findings are in ART-012. The split is deliberate and is not a filing convenience. Two reasons. First, D-001 is a decision about ENCODING — 'empty is a state the encoding must express' — and dashboard-analyst is dispatched after this agent to render the board. A rendering instruction buried inside a long findings document is a rendering instruction that gets missed; as its own registered artifact the coverage object is addressable on its own. Second, the two carry different KINDS of claim. This artifact makes claims about the study (what ran, at what tier, what did not), which a reader can check by opening the source files. ART-012 makes claims about the market, every one of them inherited at the source's stated tier and capped by the coverage here. Mixing them lets the market claims borrow the certainty of the meta claims. The risk of splitting — that ART-012 is read as complete coverage, which D-002 forbids — is answered structurally: ART-012 opens with a coverage ceiling that cites this artifact, names it in inputs.artifacts, and repeats 'of the six profiled' in every section heading that carries a market claim.
notes.citation_notation: The payload cites sources as [S-nn], NOT as [ART-nnn]. ADR-017 defines the ART form as resolving against artifacts/_registry.json, and not one of the 48 Batch 3 source files is a registered artifact. Minting artifact IDs for raw sources would be the same defect ADR-017 refused when it declined to mint ledger IDs for measurements. The S-register is declared in full inside the payload and resolves to a sha256 in research/sources-manifest.json plus a real heading in the named file. No [E-nnn] appears anywhere: the ledger holds 0 records, and a claim of the form 'users want X' is blocked here no matter how reasonable.
notes.new_workstream: luma-travel is new. The three existing workstreams (brand-foundations, design-system-selection, system-operations) are all about CoForge's own system; this is the first client-product workstream. It is NOT named luma-discovery or luma, because ADR-009 renamed this repository's own project from Luma to CoForge and a bare 'luma' directory would read as that former name. The travel product and the former project name are different things that share a word.
notes.coverage_ceiling: 6 of 14 competitors profiled. 98 of 770 planned feature cells (12.7%) rest on Tier 1 observation. 37 of 112 planned journey stage-cells (33%) carry any rating. One of the study's five designated tests — the one its own benchmark plan flags as supporting a headline opportunity — did not run.
